findings.description: query is const char* and used directly to build std::regex. If query is null, behavior is undefined and may crash.
std::regex construction throws std::regex_error on invalid patterns; no try/catch.
Passing user-controlled query directly to std::regex allows arbitrary regex features. If intent is substring search, this is direct injection.
Even if regex is intended, untrusted patterns can cause catastrophic backtracking and DoS. C++ std::regex has no timeout or guarantees against this.
Logging full file paths and snippet content (even in DEV) can leak sensitive information.
If filePath is derived from user input and not constrained, an attacker can read arbitrary files. The function performs no path validation or sandboxing.
Processing arbitrarily large files/lines and storing entire matching lines in memory can lead to memory/CPU exhaustion.
Using int for positions (offset) risks truncation for very long lines; std::smatch::position() returns a signed difference type; unsafe cast to int.
